definitions.explanation: The act of traveling to unknown or unfamiliar places to discover and investigate them. Used for both serious geographical exploration and casual, playful exploration by children.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{森|もり}→森：02260_mori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{探検|たんけん}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{南極|なんきょく}→南極：11936_nankyoku⟧{探検|たんけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦について→〜について：03103_nitsuite⟧{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んだ→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I read a book about the history of Antarctic exploration.

examples.japanese: ⟦{廃墟|はいきょ}→廃墟：12453_haikyo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{探検|たんけん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{趣味|しゅみ}→趣味：00889_shumi⟧だ⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{誘|さそ}われて→誘う：01947_sasou⟧、⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{工場|こうじょう}→工場：01082_koujou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: A friend whose hobby is exploring ruins invited me, and we entered an old factory.

notes:
USAGE:
Used for both serious expeditions (geographical, scientific) and casual adventures. Children going on neighborhood explorations and professional explorers both use this word.

The variant {探険|たんけん} (with {険|けん} meaning danger) is also used, though {探検|たんけん} (with {検|けん} meaning examine) is more standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {探検|たんけん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to explore)
- {探検|たんけん}⟦{隊|たい}→隊：03383_tai⟧ (expedition team)
- {探検|たんけん}{家|か} (explorer)
- ⟦{洞窟|どうくつ}→洞窟：05038_doukutsu⟧{探検|たんけん} (cave exploration)
- ⟦{秘境|ひきょう}→秘境：16500_hikyou⟧{探検|たんけん} (exploration of hidden regions)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{冒険|ぼうけん}→冒険：03629_bouken⟧: adventure — emphasizes risk and excitement rather than discovery
- ⟦{調査|ちょうさ}→調査：03489_chousa⟧: investigation — more systematic and scientific, less adventurous
